name: Indexer
tip: An indexer answers 'where can I find npub X'. It hands out addresses and stores no one else's posts — a phone book, not a library.

children.name: status
children.label: This device
children.tip: Whether the network is being sent here right now.

children.name: volunteer
children.label: Volunteer this device
children.tip: Off = hold nothing. Plugged in = serve while on a charger and a real uplink. Always = serve regardless. Revoking is exactly as easy as granting.

children.name: pointers
children.label: Addresses held
children.tip: An indexer holds pointers, never other people's posts.

children.name: authors
children.label: Authors this device is a home for
children.tip: Published as who-has records, so people are sent to you and not to a server.

children.name: peers
children.label: Indexers synced with
children.tip: Indexers spread the map between themselves so phones never have to.

children.name: hygiene
children.label: Dead pointers pruned · stores refused
children.tip: A provider that will not serve stops being handed out.

children.name: hardware
children.label: Hardware (change in Settings)
children.tip: Power, uplink and how much of the last week this device actually had power.

name: The network
tip: Other indexers this device knows — and the leaves it deliberately leaves alone.

children.name: network
children.tip: Leaves announce, get indexed, and are never woken. That asymmetry is why the role exists.
